items.title: Josef Balcerak Interview, 1968-05-17

ctx.x: Yes, I would like to know about it.

No, it was probably eight or nine years ago, and we arranged a special concert in Philharmonic Hall in Warsaw. And Willis Conover came as a first time. He was very surprised by the grouse, versatility, and liveliness of the Polish jazz scene. At a large jazz concert in Philharmonic, giving thanks for an enthusiastic welcome, he said, It is I who should applaud you for the dignity that you have brought to the appreciation of jazz, and you, the musicians, for devoting your lies to music so far from its source, but…

Oh, one thing I notice about it, if you don't mind my saying this, is that I think you have a very good sense of humor as well as good rhythm in your playing. Those two things stand out to me. Mm-hmm. Ragtime also, I'd say. Tell me about the Polish sense of humor.
